records.text: There had been substantial suspicion that the federal government knew that roughly 60 to 80 percent of cocaine was coming through the Douglas, Arizona area, while local authorities claimed not to know where it was coming from
records.speaker: Mitch Snow

appearances.snippet: Prior to us getting there, there had been some, a lot of suspicion that the federal government knew that 80%, I think it was 60 to 80% of the cocaine was coming through the Douglas, Arizona area... So they knew all the cocaine is coming through this one area. But the local authorities back then, you know, came up with shrugs like, you know, oh, we just don't see where it's coming from.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous and later reporting supports that the Douglas tunnel was a major cocaine route and that its discovery produced public suspicion of compromised or collaborating U.S. officials; several border agents were later convicted in other local cases. Official DOJ testimony says about one ton of cocaine moved through the 1990 tunnel. However, the reviewed sources do not support the specific assertion that 60 to 80 percent of cocaine entered through the Douglas area or document the exact claimed response by local authorities. The suspicion component is supported, while the numerical and attribution components are not.
